To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

the superimposition of a train of stimuli during maximal voluntary contraction (MVC) is a more sensitive method than either a single or double stimulus for the detection of central activation failure.
a superimposing a train of stimuli is more sensitive to detect central activation failures during isometric MVC than a single or double stimuli method.

the central activation ratio, which is the ratio of the maximum voluntary force to the maximum voluntary force plus the force generated during a supramaximal electrical stimulus, was lower when a train of stimuli was imposed during a maximal voluntary contraction than when a single stimulus or double stimulus was used.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the quantification of neuromuscular fatigue.
the development of a method for quantitating central activation during isometric maximal voluntary contraction (MVC).
the development of a quantitative method for detecting and quantifying central activation failure.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the use of high‐frequency trains of stimuli is a sensitive indicator of central fatigue.
the superimposition of a train of stimuli (50 Hz, either 500 or 1,000 ms duration) is a sensitive indicator of central fatigue during isometric MVC's in both normal and pathological subjects.

the central activation ratio is a sensitive and reliable indicator of central activation and central activation failure during voluntary contractions in healthy subjects and patients with neuromuscular diseases.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
we have shown that central activation failure during voluntary contraction can be quantitated with a superimposed train of stimuli.

we developed a novel method to quantify central activation failure during MVC in humans and we used this technique to quantify central activation in healthy subjects, in patients with amyotrophilic lateral sclerosis, and in healthy subjects after fatiguinig exercise.
the superimposed high-frequency train of stimuli is the most sensitive indicator of central failure during isometric maximal voluntary contractions.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the superimposed train of stimuli method is a more sensitive method for detecting central activation failure than either the single or the double stimuli method during MVCs of human skeletal muscle.
we found a way to quantify how well the brain can activate the muscles.
central activation failure can be detected using a superimposed train of stimuli of the nerve supplying the muscle being tested.
